The keyboard adjusts the suggestions to your typing. Nothing leaves your device

The keyboard keeps the words and the word pairs that you type in a private word list on this device. This makes the suggestions and glide typing better. The keyboard learns nothing in a password field, and nothing while incognito mode is on. You can delete the learned words below at any time.
Add words to the system dictionary
Share the learned words with the Android personal dictionary

The keyboard also saves the words that you type in the Android personal dictionary. Other keyboards and the spell checker of the system then know these words too. It is the same list that you can edit in System settings → Languages & input → Dictionary. This setting is off at the start: the keyboard has its own learning, and this setting writes outside the app. It obeys \"Learn from typing\" and incognito mode. When you turn it off, the words that are already in the list stay there.
Treat the words in the Android personal dictionary as known words

The keyboard reads the Android personal dictionary. It is the same list in System settings → Languages & input → Dictionary. Each word in that list is a known word: the keyboard suggests it, autocorrect does not change it, and the keyboard does not ask you to add it again when you type or glide it. This setting is on at the start. The keyboard reads the list again each time you change it, so a word that you add in System settings works at once. This setting only reads the list. \"Add words to the system dictionary\" is the setting that writes to it.
Type a shortcut from the Android personal dictionary to get its full phrase as a suggestion

Each entry in the Android personal dictionary can have a shortcut. It is the same list in System settings → Languages & input → Dictionary. With this setting on, you type a shortcut, for example \"omw\", and its full phrase, \"on my way\", becomes the top suggestion. This setting is on at the start. The keyboard reads the list again each time you change it, so a shortcut that you add in System settings works at once. This setting is not the snippets of the keyboard. A snippet belongs to the Snippets tool, has its own screen under Features → Text Expander, and works whether this setting is on or off.
While this setting is on, the keyboard learns nothing from your typing and keeps no clipboard history. The words that it learned before stay as they are.
Turn incognito mode on by itself in private tabs and fields

An app can mark a text field as a field that the keyboard must not learn from. Chrome does this for every field in an incognito tab. Other browsers and password managers do the same on their private screens. While such a field has the focus, the keyboard turns incognito mode on for it, and the incognito badge shows next to the toolbar. When you leave the field, typing goes back to normal. The keyboard cannot detect an app that never sends this mark. This setting does not work for a private mode of that kind.
Include the keyboard in the Android backup and in the device-to-device transfer

This setting is off at the start. The keyboard copies nothing that it stores to Google Drive or to a new device. Turn it on, and the Android backup treats the keyboard like any other app. Your settings, themes, layouts, snippets, learned words, sticker packs, icon packs and plugins come back on a new device, or after you install the app again. The backup leaves out the voice models, the AI models, the downloaded word lists and the emoji keyword packs. The keyboard can download these again by itself, and the backup must stay inside the size limit of Android. The backup does include your saved API keys. Android makes a cloud backup only on a device that can encrypt it with your screen lock. Backup & restore in Settings is the other way, and it never uses Google. It saves the same data in a file that you move yourself.
Everything the keyboard picked up from your typing

This deletes every word that the keyboard learned from you, your emoji history, the corrections that you undid, and your Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese picks. The keyboard also deletes your personal dictionary. The words that you add by hand go into the same list. Your snippets and your imported word lists stay. This cannot be undone.

Typing works fully on this device. The word lists, prediction, autocorrect, transliteration and emoji search are part of the app, and none of them needs a network connection. The app collects nothing about you and has no analytics of its own. Handwriting, text scanning and QR scanning are built on Google\'s ML Kit, which reports its own diagnostics to Google while you use them. Only a tool uses the network, and only at the moment that you press it: translate, weather, web search, image search, GIFs, stickers, dictionary lookup and the AI tools. You can turn off each one of them on the Tools screen.
Ask for your fingerprint before the screens and the delete buttons that you pick
Turning this on and off also asks for your fingerprint

The keyboard asks for your fingerprint before it opens the screens that you tick below, and before it runs the delete buttons that you tick. It asks again before you can turn this setting off, so somebody holding your unlocked phone cannot simply switch it off.

This is a lock on the screens, not encryption. It does not change how anything is stored. A settings export, the Android backup, a computer with USB debugging on, and a rooted phone all still reach the same data, and the keyboard itself keeps working as before. What the lock stops is the case it is for: somebody who picks up your unlocked phone for half a minute.

If you remove every fingerprint from this phone, the lock stands aside and the screens open normally. There is then nothing to check against, and you must never be shut out of your own settings.
One check opens every locked screen until this time is up. A delete button always asks again, however recently you answered, because that check is the last step before something goes away for good.
Accept the PIN, pattern or password of this phone as well as a fingerprint

Keep this on unless you have a reason not to. It is the way back in when the fingerprint reader locks itself out after too many tries, and it is the only way this works at all on a phone with no reader. Turn it off and a fingerprint is the only answer the lock accepts.
You chose to lock this. Confirm that this is you to open it.
Too many tries. Wait about 30 seconds, then try again.
Too many tries. Unlock this phone with your PIN, pattern or password, then come back.
The check did not work. Try again.
This phone has no fingerprint and no screen lock set up, so there is nothing to check against. The lock stands aside until you add one.
This phone has no fingerprint reader that the app can use, so the lock stands aside.
The fingerprint reader is busy. Try again in a moment.
Open the system settings to add a fingerprint or a screen lock
The lock hides these screens inside this app. It does not encrypt them. A settings export, the Android backup, a computer with USB debugging on and a rooted phone all still read the same data.
Ask the system to check a fingerprint for the lock in Privacy. The app never sees the fingerprint itself
See what the keyboard can reach, and give or take back a permission

The keyboard works without all of these permissions. Each one unlocks one optional feature. Press a row to give the permission. Press a granted row to open the system settings, where you can take it back.
Dictate text with the voice input tool
Take a photo with the camera tool and send it into the chat
Suggest the names and the email addresses of your contacts while you type
The calendar tool lists the events of your day
Show your new screenshots in the clipboard
Save images from the keyboard to your gallery
Media controls on the keyboard, and one-time codes from your notifications
Show which app a clipboard entry was copied from
Keep the keyboard gestures while TalkBack is on
Only the network tools use it: translate, weather, search, GIFs, stickers, dictionary and the AI tools
The model downloads first check that the connection is not metered
Haptic feedback when you press a key

Android gives the permissions in the last group to every app at the install. An app cannot ask for them, and cannot give them back. You can take every other permission back at any time in the system settings. The feature that uses it then stops, and the rest of the keyboard keeps working.
